body:
Hello! I think I know why it doesn't work at the moment:
Gamecube HIDAPI driver calls a function to enable gamecube adaptors here:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/3911e0963d39b79a85cb329340c6918397d2d05e/thirdparty/sdl/joystick/hidapi/SDL_hidapi_gamecube.c#L104-L117
It's guarded by `HAVE_ENABLE_GAMECUBE_ADAPTORS` definition, which we don't have at the moment.
Here's the function itself:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/3911e0963d39b79a85cb329340c6918397d2d05e/thirdparty/sdl/hidapi/SDL_hidapi.c#L1697-L1752
It's also guarded by `HAVE_LIBUSB`, which we also don't have.
It also checks if the device's vendor/product IDs are 0x057e and 0x0337 respectively, which are, I assume, the ones from the official Nintendo adapter:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/3911e0963d39b79a85cb329340c6918397d2d05e/thirdparty/sdl/hidapi/SDL_hidapi.c#L880-L893

Theoretically, if we define `HAVE_ENABLE_GAMECUBE_ADAPTORS` and `HAVE_LIBUSB` in `drivers/sdl/SDL_build_config_private.h` (our SDL configuration) for Linux, the official Nintendo adapter should work. I will create a PR for that soon!
